The G-7 agreed a 100M-barrel release with diesel front-loaded -- a government aiming at the refiners' margin while MPC, VLO and PSX trade above their mean targets (wiki/energy.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 1).

why: XLE is one of three ETFs above its 50-day and one of five above its 200-day; the range held at both edges (wiki/synthesis.md Section 2).

The diesel shortage is physical: a crack reported above $100/bbl, and the energy desk doubts 0.8 mb/d for four months closes a gap made by shipping, strikes and an export ban (wiki/energy.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 6).
Month RF cut 55 -> 52 and MC cut 50 -> 45: the stance is hold-add-nothing and policy now targets the margin.
risks: SLB -5.4 pct is the dissent inside the sector; the failed breakout below $63.46 still stands (wiki/energy.md).
If the G-7 release works, the refiner leg (15.8 pct of XLE) mean-reverts from near-record prices; VLO prints Oct 22 (wiki/synthesis.md Sections 1 and 5).
Falsifier: WTI below $88.06 with a close under $60.95; bullish above $96.54 (wiki/synthesis.md Section 5).

extracts.lead_summary: Crude went down and the sector went up, and the reason is in the product, not the barrel. WTI slipped to $91.11 (-$1.30) and the G-7 agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels — with diesel front-loaded in the first twenty days, because diesel is the shortage. Refiners took back everything last week's diplomacy cost them: MPC +7.3% to within a dollar of its record, VLO +4.9%, PSX +3.5%. XLE closed $62.82 (+1.3%) after Tuesday's $60.95 low undercut the 50-day and reversed — still under the $63.46 breakout line, so the failed breakout stands, but the breakdown did not follow. SLB (-5.4%) is the dissent. OPEC+ meets tomorrow, after this page is written.
